key_insight: Large language models can help detect outcome switching in clinical trial reports by comparing intended vs reported outcomes and classifying semantic similarity.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster screening of trial publications for spin, which matters because misleading outcome reporting is common in randomized trials and can affect how results are interpreted.
method: Trained on 300 labeled outcome pairs for semantic similarity
Compared baseline text-similarity methods with open-source LLMs
Used prompt engineering, token-probability classification, and majority voting to make the final decision
evidence_signal: On a 2,496-example test set, the approach reached F1 0.78 and accuracy 0.90, outperforming baseline similarity models but not fine-tuned BERT.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but the system still trails supervised BERT variants and would need careful validation before real-world use.
paper_title: Detecting Spin in Clinical Trials with Large Language Models
